identityReview: Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif, also spelled Shahbaz; born 23 September 1951, Lahore origin, Government College Lahore graduate. Different from brother Nawaz and son Hamza. Current Pakistani premier, former Punjab chief minister with 2009 interruption and former National Assembly opposition leader. No unsupported degree, graduation year, current party presidency, exact 2013 disputed transition date or prime-minister ordinal.
lifeStatusEvidence: Actual 12 November 2026 Antalya meeting with Erdoğan during COP31 reported the same day by Türkiye and the next day by Pakistan MOIB. Meeting date is distinguished from Pakistan publication date.

sourceReview.accessMethod: Read Punjab CM list and selected provincial assembly notifications, Toronto consular biography, original 2022 and 2024 National Assembly proceedings, IMF SBA and EFF Board announcements, relevant AP election body, Turkish and Pakistani official completed-meeting accounts. Read Commons crop/root metadata, original COP29 gallery text and presidential website CC BY 4.0 permission. No image pixels.
corrections: Punjab official list gives birth 23 September 1951 and Lahore as place of origin, plus chief-minister periods 20 February 1997–12 October 1999, 8 June 2008–27 March 2013 and 7 June 2013–7 June 2018. It omits the 2009 interruption. Provincial assembly decisions separately cite 6 June 2013 assumption, a one-day discrepancy: profile uses 2013 year precision rather than choosing an unsupported exact date. Third-term endpoint is also kept at year precision.

Toronto consulate heading confirms oath on 4 March 2024 and prior premiership April 2022–August 2023. Read Government College Lahore graduation, 1985 chamber presidency, provincial assembly 1988, National Assembly 1990, provincial opposition 1993 and chief-minister history. No subject, degree level or graduation year given. Older body says opposition leader and party president from 2018 to April 2022: not evidence of current party presidency or opposition role. Nawaz is his brother, a different premier. Promotional adjectives are omitted.

Original National Assembly proceedings of 11 April 2022 record election with 174 votes, announced at 5:02 pm. Qureshi had announced withdrawal; zero votes recorded for him are not interpreted as a universal vote against his party. Document confirms parliamentary election, not a separate oath ceremony. First-term end is only August 2023 from consulate; no invented exact end date.

Original National Assembly proceedings of 3 March 2024 record 201 for Sharif and 92 for Omer Ayub, with declaration at 1:43 pm. Parliamentary voting, election declaration and next-day oath are distinct. Avoids inconsistent ordinal prime-minister numbering and does not represent these as nationwide popular votes.

Read IMF 12 July 2023 Board announcement: nine-month SBA of SDR2.250 billion, approximately US$3 billion; SDR894 million/about US$1.2 billion immediately available, remainder phased subject to two quarterly reviews. Approval is not full payment, a grant or personal wealth. Distinct from 2024 EFF.

Read IMF release dated 27 September 2024 covering Board action on 25 September: 37-month EFF of SDR5.320 billion/about US$7 billion; SDR760 million/about US$1 billion immediately available. Fiscal, energy and governance reforms, social protection and continuing vulnerabilities are noted; no assertion that all funds arrived immediately, debt problems ended or forecasts became actual 2026 results.

Read AP 2024 election report for coalition context, first premiership after Imran Khan government fell, and PTI allegations about the preceding general election alongside election-authority denial. Allegations are not adopted as proven fraud or a judicial verdict. The official parliamentary tally is independently confirmed by primary proceedings.

Read Turkish presidency communications account dated 12 November 2026: actual Erdoğan–Sharif meeting in Antalya during COP31. This is a completed encounter, not merely a travel itinerary. No unverified wider diplomatic or peace-settlement claims imported.

Read Pakistan MOIB report published 13 November 2026 describing previous Thursday’s meeting, 12 November, and trade, investment, defence, energy and connectivity discussion. Reproduces prime-minister-office information; it is Pakistan’s official account rather than an independent press eyewitness. Combined with Turkish record for reciprocal confirmation. Intentions and planned cooperation are not completed projects.

Read selected chief-minister notes in Punjab Assembly Decisions 2000–2014, printed pp. xxviii–xxix, with government notification references: 8 June 2008 assumption; Governor’s Rule introduced 25 February 2009 caused ministers to cease office, revoked 30 March. Revocation is not automatically the exact personal reinstatement date. Document gives 6 June 2013 for renewed office versus 7 June on modern CM list; profile retains year precision. Full 2015 compilation not exhaustively reviewed.

translationReview.scope: All 32 display fields across seven foreign languages checked for 1951 birth, unspecified degree details, brother distinction, provincial/federal roles and 2009 interruption, 174 votes in 2022 versus 201/92 on 3 March 2024 and 4 March oath, historical opposition office, nine-month 2023 SBA US$3 billion/US$1.2 billion versus 37-month 2024 EFF US$7 billion/US$1 billion, approval versus release and disbursement, attributed election allegations and denial, and actual 12 November 2026 meeting versus future project intentions.
